title: Wyoming LLC Pros and Cons: Why Forming Your LLC in Wyoming Could Be the Best Choice
summary: Wyoming is a popular state to form your LLC. In fact, Wyoming invented the LLC structure. Ready to get started? Our guide has all the Wyoming LLC pros and cons.
body_markdown:
A Wyoming LLC costs $100 to form and $60 a year to maintain, keeps member and manager names off public state filings, and carries no state income tax. Those are genuine advantages, and they explain much of Wyoming’s appeal. But they don’t make it the right choice for every business.


The real question isn’t simply why you should form an LLC in Wyoming. It’s whether Wyoming makes sense for where and how your business actually operates.


Before you read on, it’s worth weighing Wyoming LLC pros and cons, and if these align with the needs of your business.


If you run your business from an office, warehouse or home in another US state, a Wyoming LLC will cost you two sets of fees and save you nothing. If you are outside the US with no US footprint, or you actually live in Wyoming, the case is strong.


**Is Wyoming Right For You?**


**Wyoming is the right choice if:**


-


You live outside the US and have no US office address, employees, or inventory
-


You already live and operate in Wyoming. You run an online business with no fixed US location


**Wyoming is not the answer if:**


-


**You operate in another US state:** Register there, or you will pay two sets of fees and still owe the same tax at home.
-


**You are raising venture capital:** Investors generally prefer a Delaware C-corporation.


**What it costs:** $100 to register, then $60 a year to maintain, for the[Annual Report License tax](https://sos.wyo.gov/business/docs/businessfees.pdf) , which is $60 or $0.0002 per dollar of your Wyoming assets, whichever is greater. Any LLC with $300,000 or less in Wyoming assets pays $60. An EIN is free.


This guide takes a balanced approach. It covers the genuine benefits of a Wyoming LLC, the disadvantages other guides skip, the costs beyond the initial filing fee, and the situations where another state is the better choice.


## Wyoming LLC Benefits: Why Entrepreneurs Choose the State


Wyoming has a long list of benefits attached to its name online. Only a few consistently survive a closer look: it’s inexpensive, it keeps ownership off the state’s standard public filings, and its LLC laws have been around for nearly 50 years.


The other benefits get repeated frequently online but are either shared by many states or depend heavily on your circumstances. We’ll separate those claims from the reality below.


### Low Formation and Maintenance Cost


Wyoming charges $100 to file Articles of Organization and $60 per year to keep an LLC in good standing. Of the commonly cited advantages of a Wyoming LLC, this is one of the easiest to verify.


The cost advantage becomes more apparent when compared with states such as Nevada, which can cost roughly $425 in the first year and $350 annually thereafter, or Delaware, where LLCs face an annual franchise tax in addition to the initial formation fee.

### Ownership Stays Off The Public Record


Wyoming does not list LLC members or managers in the Articles of Organization or annual report. The public filing generally identifies the registered agent, registered office address, and person signing the filing.


Of all the advantages of a Wyoming LLC, this is the one entrepreneurs most often cite, and it is also the one most often overstated. It provides meaningful state-level privacy, but it does not make ownership anonymous.


The privacy section below sets out exactly what it does and does not cover.


### Mature LLC Statutes


Wyoming was the first US state to enact LLC legislation, doing so in 1977. Its LLC statutes have since developed into a well-established legal framework.


That history matters less for a straightforward single-member online business than some marketing claims suggest. But for entrepreneurs dealing with more complex ownership or operating structures, a mature and established LLC framework can be a genuine advantage.


### No State Income Tax And No Franchise Tax


Wyoming imposes no state corporate income tax, no individual state income tax, and no franchise tax on LLCs.


This is one of the top benefits of a Wyoming LLC, and one of the easiest to misunderstand. Forming in Wyoming does not automatically eliminate state taxes elsewhere.


An LLC is generally a pass-through entity by default, meaning its income is typically reported by its owners and taxed according to the applicable rules based on factors such as residency and income source.


### Fewer Formalities And Flexible Ownership


Wyoming LLCs generally face fewer corporate-style formalities than corporations. There is no statutory requirement for annual member meetings or corporate-style minutes, and members and managers do not have to be US citizens or Wyoming residents.


LLCs can also have perpetual duration and offer flexibility in transferring membership interests, subject to the operating agreement and applicable law.


[Wyoming also permits series LLCs](https://www.doola.com/blog/what-is-a-series-llc/) and the close LLC, a structure designed for smaller, closely held businesses with more restricted transferability. Neither is a liability shield or protection product; both are organizational structures with specific use cases.


### If You Are Forming A Corporation Instead


The benefits of incorporating in Wyoming are broadly similar on cost and taxation: the state charges the same $100 formation fee, uses an asset-based annual license tax, and does not impose a state corporate income tax.


The benefits of Wyoming corporation formation differ primarily in the area of governance. Corporations generally come with more formal management and record-keeping requirements, while LLCs offer greater structural flexibility.


**Key Takeaway:** The real benefits of forming a Wyoming LLC are cost, a quieter public record, and mature statutes. Every other benefit is either shared with most states or overstated.


## What a Wyoming LLC Costs


The benefits of a Wyoming LLC are easier to evaluate when you look at the actual numbers. Wyoming’s costs are straightforward, and the state publishes the core fees itself.


Item Cost


Articles of Organization $100


Online card processing fee 2.4%, $1 minimum


EIN $0


Annual report licence tax $60 minimum


Registered agent Varies by provider


Wyoming charges an annual report license tax of $60 or $0.0002 per dollar of assets located and employed in the state, whichever is greater. Assets outside Wyoming are excluded, so businesses with $300,000 or less in Wyoming assets pay the $60 minimum.


For most small businesses and non-US-resident-owned online businesses, that means $100 to form and $60 a year to maintain the LLC, plus the cost of a registered agent.


The annual report is due on the first day of your formation anniversary month and can be filed up to 120 days early. If you fail to file within 60 days of the deadline, the LLC is administratively dissolved. Reinstatement costs $100.


## What Wyoming Privacy Means


Wyoming LLC privacy comes down to one important distinction: what the public can see is not the same as what the government,[your bank linked to the LLC](https://www.doola.com/go-slash-banking/) , or a court can access.


State public-record rules govern the information disclosed in Wyoming business filings. Federal disclosure rules govern information reported to the US Treasury. These systems operate independently.


### State Public Records


Wyoming does not list members or managers in public LLC filings. Ownership does not become a searchable public record by default, which is genuinely unusual among US states and is the single strongest item in this state’s favour.


### What Wyoming Privacy Does Not Cover


It does not provide anonymity from:


- **The IRS** , which knows the EIN’s responsible party and receives the LLC’s tax filings.


- **Banks** , which identify beneficial owners when accounts are opened under[FinCEN’s 2016 Customer Due Diligence Rule](https://www.fincen.gov/system/files/2026-02/FinCEN-Order-CCDExceptiveRelief.pdf) .


- **Courts** , which can obtain ownership information through discovery and subpoenas.


- **Other states** , where a foreign-qualified Wyoming LLC becomes subject to that state’s public-record and disclosure requirements.


### Federal Beneficial Ownership Reporting


Under the Corporate Transparency Act, FinCEN originally required both US and foreign entities to report beneficial ownership information. That no longer applies to US-formed companies.


FinCEN issued an interim rule in March 2025 and then a[final rule on 11 August 2026](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0603) , effective 14 August 2026, permanently exempting all entities created in the United States and their beneficial owners from reporting BOI.


The rule turns on where the entity was formed, not who owns it, so a Wyoming LLC owned entirely by a non-US resident is a domestically formed entity and exempt.


FinCEN has also said it will delete previously reported US-person data.


**Key Takeaway:** Wyoming gives you a quieter public record, not invisibility. Ownership stays off the state database and remains fully visible to the IRS, courts, and also any bank you deal with.


## Asset Protection: What Charging Orders Do and Don’t Do


Charging order protection is the remedy a creditor of an individual member gets against that member’s LLC interest. It reaches distributions when they are made. It does not hand the creditor management rights or force a liquidation. Wyoming provides it by statute as the exclusive remedy for a judgment creditor of a member.


There are two important qualifications in this case:


- **Single-member LLCs are the weak spot:** Charging-order protection was historically designed in part to protect the interests of other LLC members from an outsider’s creditor. Courts have not been completely uniform in how they apply that protection when there are no other members to protect.


- **Wyoming is not unique:** Charging-order protection exists in many states, so claims that it is available only in Wyoming and a handful of other states are misleading. The details and strength of the protection vary by state.


More importantly, the biggest threats to LLC liability protection usually have little to do with the state where you formed the company. Veil piercing is more likely to become an issue when owners blur the line between themselves and the business.


For example, by commingling personal and business funds, undercapitalizing the company, ignoring the operating agreement, or failing to maintain separate business records and finances.


A Wyoming LLC operated through the owner’s personal checking account is not meaningfully protected by its Wyoming address. Conversely, an LLC formed elsewhere and operated as a genuinely separate business can have strong liability protection.


## Disadvantages of a Wyoming LLC


Wyoming’s reputation can make it easy to focus on what you gain and overlook what you add. The disadvantages of Wyoming LLC formation are especially relevant if you don’t actually live or operate there.


### You Pay Twice If You Operate Elsewhere


This is the biggest of the downsides of Wyoming LLC formation. If you run the business from another state, you may have to register the Wyoming LLC there as a foreign entity too.


That can mean two state filings, two annual reports, two registered agents, and two sets of compliance obligations, while still owing your home state the taxes it would have charged you anyway.


For instance, an entrepreneur operating from Georgia doesn’t get a Georgia tax discount for putting “Wyoming” on the formation certificate.


#### Georgia LLC vs Wyoming LLC: What the Wyoming Route Actually Costs

Form the LLC $110 $100


Georgia Certificate of Authority (foreign qualification) Not required $235


Wyoming certificate of good standing is required as an attachment to the Georgia filing Not required $0 online, $20 certified


Georgia annual registration $60 / year $60 / year, once qualified


Wyoming annual report license tax Not applicable $60 / year


Registered agent One, in Georgia. A Georgia resident can serve as their own at no cost Two, in Georgia and Wyoming. The Wyoming agent has to be a paid commercial provider, since you have no Wyoming address


Filing deadlines to track One, in Georgia (1 January – 1 April) Two, on unrelated calendars. Georgia by 1 April, Wyoming on the first day of your formation anniversary month


Consequence of missing one Administrative dissolution in Georgia Administrative dissolution in either state. Wyoming allows 60 days past the due date


Georgia income tax on the owner’s share of profit Flat rate for 2026 Same flat rate. Forming in Wyoming does not reduce it


State filing fees, year one $110 $335


Recurring state filing fees $60 / year $120 / year


Five-year state filing fees $350 $815


Figures verified against the[Georgia Secretary of State Corporations Division fee schedule](https://sos.ga.gov/how-to-guide/filing-fees-and-expedited-processing-document-filings) effective 6 September 2025, the Wyoming Secretary of State fee schedule effective 1 July 2026, and the Georgia Department of Revenue.


**The Wyoming route costs about $465 more over five years,** doubles your annual filings, and removes nothing from the Georgia column.


Registered agent service, local occupational tax certificates, and expedite fees are excluded because they vary by provider and county. Neither Georgia nor Wyoming charges a franchise tax on LLCs.


They now pay two states instead of one and maintain two sets of filings on unrelated calendars. And they owe precisely the same Georgia tax as if the LLC had been formed in Georgia for a single fee.


### Forming In Wyoming Does Not Avoid State Tax Or Nexus


A Wyoming formation certificate does not really determine where you’re taxable. If you have an office, employees, inventory, or an owner working from home in another state, you may have a physical nexus there. If you cross[certain sales thresholds](https://www.doola.com/blog/sales-tax-by-state-economic-nexus-state-guide/) , you might have an ‘economic nexus’.


Either way, the state where the activity happens can still impose its own registration and tax requirements. Wyoming’s tax structure doesn’t cancel them.


### The Bank May Ask, “Where Do You Actually Operate?”


Some banks and[payment processors like Stripe](https://www.doola.com/go-stripeatlas/) may scrutinize an LLC that has little or no apparent connection to its state of formation. This is particularly relevant when an entrepreneur uses the registered agent’s address as though it were the company’s operating address.


A registered agent address is for receiving official legal and state correspondence. It does not automatically establish where your business operates. Misrepresenting it as your business address can create verification problems.


And while choosing a different formation state may reduce some friction, no formation provider can guarantee approval by a particular bank or payment processor.


### Form 5472 For Foreign-Owned Single-Member LLCs


For a foreign-owned single-member LLC that is treated as a disregarded entity for federal tax purposes, the compliance burden doesn’t end when the LLC is formed.


The business generally[must file Form 5472](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f5472--2018.pdf) with a pro forma Form 1120 each year, reporting certain transactions between the LLC and its foreign owner, including reportable capital contributions and distributions.


The penalty for failing to file Form 5472 correctly can be $25,000. This requirement can apply even when the LLC has no revenue and owes no US income tax. A dormant foreign-owned LLC may still have a filing obligation.


### You Don’t Have Much Time to Fix a “Missed” Annual Report


Wyoming’s annual report deadline comes with a relatively short cure period. An LLC that misses its annual report deadline can become delinquent and, if the report remains unfiled, be administratively dissolved **60 days after the due date** .


That makes the annual report a small task with potentially disproportionate consequences: miss it, and you can put the entity’s good standing at risk surprisingly quickly.


### “Private” Doesn’t Mean Anonymous


Wyoming keeps member and manager names off its standard public filings. That’s useful. But it doesn’t hide ownership from banks, the IRS, courts, or other parties with legal authority to access it.


If you chose Wyoming expecting **anonymity everywhere** , you’re paying for a benefit the state doesn’t actually provide.

## Why You Shouldn’t Form an LLC in Wyoming


While Wyoming is a strong choice for some businesses, here are four cases where it’s better to form elsewhere.


- **You physically operate in another US state:** Form there. Foreign qualification will add a second set of ‘fees and filings’ to your home-state obligations that were never reduced.


- **You are raising institutional venture capital:** A Delaware C corporation is generally the conventional structure for institutional VC. Starting with an LLC can mean a more complicated conversion later, potentially at the least convenient point in your company’s growth.


- **Your business is genuinely local:** If your customers, premises and staff are all in one state, forming there is better than creating an unnecessary Wyoming connection.


- **You are buying property in another state:** For real estate, the “Wyoming LLC benefits real estate” argument is often overstated. When an LLC is being used to hold property, the state where the property sits generally matters far more because that’s where the property is recorded, regulated, and potentially litigated.


Wyoming isn’t a workaround for where your business actually operates. If your business, investors, or assets point clearly to another state, form your LLC in that state.


## Wyoming LLC for Non-US Residents


No US citizenship, residency, Social Security number[or US address](https://www.doola.com/go-virtualpostmail/) is required to own or form a Wyoming LLC. Also, Wyoming imposes no “residency requirement” on members or managers.


For entrepreneurs based outside the US with **no US office, employees, or inventory** , this is where Wyoming’s reputation starts to make sense. The state offers a low $100 formation fee, a $60 annual minimum license tax, and a public filing that does not list LLC members or managers.


But don’t mistake easy formation for easy compliance. The more important considerations come after formation:


- The EIN comes from the IRS[on Form SS-4](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf) , filed by fax or mail with “Foreign” as the responsible party identifier where there is no SSN or ITIN.


- An ITIN is a personal tax ID and is needed only where the individual has a US filing obligation of their own; many non-resident owners never need one.


- Form 5472 is the annual obligation most often missed, at a $25,000 penalty.


**Important structural limitation:** A nonresident alien generally cannot be an S corporation shareholder. As a result, an S corporation election is generally unavailable to non-US-resident owners, regardless of the LLC’s state of formation.


## The Verdict: Is a Wyoming LLC Worth It?


Weighing the pros and cons of a Wyoming LLC comes down to these four ‘conditional’ answers:


- You live outside the US with no US office, employees or inventory: Yes, Wyoming is a strong default on cost and public record.


- You live and operate in Wyoming: Yes, form in Wyoming.


- You physically operate in another US state: No, form where you operate.


- You are raising institutional venture capital: No, expect a Delaware C-corporation.


For the entrepreneurs it fits, $100 and $60 a year buys a genuinely low-maintenance entity with a quieter public record than almost any other state offers. For everyone else, it simply adds a second set of fees, filings, and compliance to the stack.

## FAQs


### What are the pros and cons of a Wyoming LLC?


**Pros:** $100 to form, a $60 minimum annual license tax, no members or managers listed on standard public filings, no state personal or corporate income tax, and established LLC laws.


**Cons:** if you operate somewhere else, you may end up paying and filing in two states, and Wyoming’s privacy does not make your ownership invisible to banks, the IRS, or courts.


### Is a Wyoming LLC really anonymous?


No, Wyoming does not name members or managers in public state filings, which keeps ownership out of a casual search. It does not conceal ownership from the IRS, a court, a subpoena,[or a bank running](https://www.doola.com/go-slash-banking/) customer due diligence at account opening.


### Do I need to live in Wyoming to form a Wyoming LLC?


No, Wyoming does not impose residency or citizenship requirements. You do need a registered agent with a physical Wyoming street address, and if you physically operate in another US state you will also need to register there.


### How much does a Wyoming LLC cost per year?


$60, the minimum annual report licence tax, for any LLC with $300,000 or less in assets located and employed in Wyoming.


Above that, the tax is $0.0002 per dollar of Wyoming assets. Registered agent service is priced separately.


### What happens if I miss the Wyoming annual report?


Wyoming charges no late fee, but the entity goes delinquent on day two of the month following the due date and is administratively dissolved if the report is not filed within 60 days of the due date. Reinstatement is $100.


### Can a non-US resident form a Wyoming LLC?


Yes, they can. No citizenship, residency, SSN or US address is required.


Get the EIN by fax or mail on Form SS-4 with “Foreign” as the responsible party identifier.


Foreign-owned single-member LLCs must file Form 5472 annually, with a $25,000 penalty for failure to file.
